hints: Focus on where the new hydrogen atom actually goes when an aldehyde C=O is reduced to an alcohol.
Track the two hydrogens on the carbon of compound Z, one original 1H from ethanal and one new 3H from NaBH4.
Consider what happens on oxidation when only one of those two C-H hydrogens is removed, given 1H and 3H behave identically.
walkthrough:
**Identify compound Z**

Reduction of ethanal gives ethanol, a primary alcohol. Think of it as adding H across the C=O bond.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + 2[\text{H}] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Label the hydrogens in Z**

The carbonyl carbon in $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ already has one $^1\text{H}$. Nucleophilic $^3\text{H}^-$ from $\text{NaBH}_4$ adds to that carbon.

So Z is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(^1\text{H})(^3\text{H})\text{OH}$. The carbon now carries both isotopes, while the O-H hydrogen comes from work-up and is $^1\text{H}$.

**Recall what oxidation removes**

Oxidation of a primary alcohol back to an aldehyde removes two H atoms, one from carbon and one from oxygen, to make water.

$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O} + [\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**See the two equally likely paths**

Because $^1\text{H}$ and $^3\text{H}$ have the same chemistry, either C-H can be removed. If the $^1\text{H}$ is removed, the $^3\text{H}$ stays on the new ethanal. If the $^3\text{H}$ is removed, it goes into the new water with the O-H $^1\text{H}$. Across many molecules, both labelled ethanal and labelled water are formed.

options.A: Correct. The mixture contains both outcomes. Some Z molecules lose 1H from carbon to give CH3C(3H)O, and others lose 3H from carbon to give H(3H)O. So as a bulk sample, both ethanal and water contain 3H.
options.B: Incorrect. This assumes the 3H always stays on carbon. In fact the C-H bond is broken on oxidation, so in half the molecules the 3H is lost from carbon into water.
options.C: Incorrect. This ignores the label completely. The 3H added in reduction cannot vanish, it must end up in either the regenerated ethanal or the water.
options.D: Incorrect. This assumes the 3H is always removed from carbon. In fact removal is random, so in half the molecules the original 1H is removed instead and the 3H remains to give labelled ethanal.
